12.ai_answer: Without specific income and tax payment figures for Mr. Gribbon and Mr. Doyle provided in the visible portion of the document, a complete analysis requires calculating their effective tax rates (tax paid ÷ income × 100). A tax system is: PROGRESSIVE if the tax rate increases as income increases (higher earners pay a larger percentage); PROPORTIONAL (flat) if everyone pays the same percentage regardless of income; REGRESSIVE if lower-income individuals pay a higher percentage of their income than higher-income individuals. To determine which applies, compare the effective tax rates: if the higher earner has a higher rate, it's progressive; if rates are equal, it's proportional; if the lower earner has a higher rate, it's regressive. Progressive taxation is based on the ability-to-pay principle and aims to reduce income inequality.
